zh.title: 小松機場跑道裂損一度關閉　長榮BR158空中等待後折返桃園
zh.summary: 日本小松機場10月5日上午因跑道裂損一度關閉，長榮BR158接近小松後無法降落，空中等待後折返桃園，約中午12時21分返抵臺灣。
body: 日本石川縣小松機場（KMQ）今（5）日上午因跑道發現裂損一度全面關閉，造成多架原定抵達航班改降、折返或取消。由臺灣出發的長榮航空BR158也受到影響，班機飛抵日本附近空域後無法降落，在空中等待一段時間後最終放棄前往小松，折返臺灣桃園國際機場（TPE）。
航空自衛隊小松基地表示，當地上午約9時40分在跑道發現異物，後續檢查確認跑道鋪面出現影響航空器運作的損壞。日本國土交通省資料顯示，裂損範圍約為縱橫40公分、深約4公分，跑道自當地時間上午10時40分左右開始關閉，由自衛隊進行緊急修復。
BR158原訂臺北時間上午6時35分由桃園起飛、日本時間上午10時25分抵達小松，當日由Airbus A330-300執飛。航班資料顯示，班機實際於上午約6時56分離開桃園，在接近小松後受到跑道關閉影響，最終未能於目的地降落。
航班追蹤資料將今日BR158列為改降／折返航班，原目的地為小松，但最後返回桃園，約於臺北時間中午12時21分抵達。從原先上午起飛至重新返回桃園，旅客在機上歷時超過5小時，形成一趟未實際進入日本的長時間往返飛行。
值得注意的是，網路上有說法稱BR158在小松附近等待至「最低油量」後才返航，但目前公開的官方資料及主要航班追蹤來源並未證實機組曾宣告minimum fuel或燃油進入特定警戒狀態，因此不宜直接將此說法視為已確認事實。同樣地，桃園是否原先即被列為該航班的正式備降機場，目前亦無公開飛行計畫資料可以證實。
小松機場其後完成跑道修復。日本航空與當地媒體資料顯示，跑道於日本時間下午1時34分左右恢復使用，較早期預估的下午3時40分提前約2小時。此次事件共造成至少10架次航班取消、改降或其他營運異動，包括由東京羽田機場（HND）前往小松的日本航空航班改降名古屋中部國際機場（NGO）、全日空航班則改降富山市富山機場（TOY）。
由於BR158在跑道重新開放前已決定返回桃園，即使小松機場隨後恢復運作，該班機仍需由長榮航空重新安排後續運送方式。旅客是否可依旅遊不便險申請班機延誤、行程更改或其他給付，則須依各保單對「折返原機場」、「延誤時間」及後續補飛安排的定義判斷，不能僅因班機折返便一概認定符合特定理賠項目。

en.title: Komatsu Airport Runway Damage Forces Temporary Closure; EVA Air BR158 Holds Before Returning to Taoyuan
en.summary: Komatsu Airport temporarily closed its runway on October 5 after pavement damage was discovered. EVA Air flight BR158 was unable to land after reaching the area, held in the air, and ultimately returned to Taiwan Taoyuan.
body: Komatsu Airport (KMQ) in Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan, temporarily closed its runway on the morning of October 5 after damage was discovered, forcing several inbound flights to divert, return to their departure airports or be canceled. EVA Air flight BR158 from Taiwan was also affected. After reaching airspace near Komatsu and being unable to land, the aircraft remained airborne for a period before abandoning the approach and returning to Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport (TPE).

Japan Air Self-Defense Force's Komatsu Air Base said a foreign object was found on the runway at around 9:40 a.m. local time, and a subsequent inspection confirmed pavement damage significant enough to affect aircraft operations. According to Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, the damaged area measured roughly 40 by 40 centimeters and about 4 centimeters deep. The runway was closed from around 10:40 a.m. while emergency repairs were carried out by the Self-Defense Forces.

BR158 was scheduled to depart Taoyuan at 6:35 a.m. Taipei time and arrive at Komatsu at 10:25 a.m. Japan time, with an Airbus A330-300 operating the flight. Flight data indicates that the aircraft actually departed Taoyuan at about 6:56 a.m. and later approached the Komatsu area, but the runway closure prevented it from landing at its destination.

Flight-tracking services list BR158 as a diverted or return flight. Although Komatsu was the original destination, the aircraft ultimately returned to Taoyuan and landed at approximately 12:21 p.m. Taipei time. From its morning departure until its return, passengers spent more than five hours aboard the aircraft on a round trip that never resulted in an arrival in Japan.

Some online posts claimed BR158 remained near Komatsu until reaching 'minimum fuel' before turning back. However, publicly available official information and major flight-tracking sources do not confirm that the crew declared minimum fuel or entered any specific fuel-alert condition. That claim should therefore not be treated as established fact. Likewise, there is no publicly available flight-plan information confirming whether Taoyuan had originally been designated as the flight's formal alternate airport.

Komatsu Airport later completed runway repairs. Japan Airlines and local media reported that the runway reopened at around 1:34 p.m. Japan time, roughly two hours earlier than an initial estimate of 3:40 p.m. The disruption caused at least 10 flights to be canceled, diverted or otherwise affected. Among them, a Japan Airlines flight from Tokyo Haneda (HND) to Komatsu diverted to Chubu Centrair International Airport (NGO), while an All Nippon Airways service diverted to Toyama Airport (TOY).

Because BR158 had already decided to return to Taoyuan before the runway reopened, EVA Air still needed to arrange onward transportation for affected passengers. Whether travelers qualify for flight-delay, itinerary-change or other travel-insurance benefits depends on the wording of each policy, including how it defines a return to the origin airport, the length of the delay and any subsequent replacement flight. A return to the departure airport alone does not automatically establish eligibility for a particular insurance payout.
